newsitem.title: BERMUDA: NZ SPORT - Dedicated Puma flanker earns test spot.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT - Dedicated Puma flanker earns test spot.

text.p: HAMILTON, June 26 - Argentine rugby player Roberto Travaglini's bloodline was always going to make him a sporting thoroughbred from the pampas.
His uncles Alejandro and Gabriel Travaglini played rugby for Argentina over three decades from the 1960s.

Twenty-three-year-old Travaglini has played three tests himself, but none will compare with his appearance for the Pumas in his first full-blooded international, against the All Blacks on Saturday, NZPA reports.
"I will always remember my first cap but the All Blacks is my first big game, the real test match," Travaglini said.
He is one of the three changes to the Pumas team, licking their wounded pride after their record 93-8 first test loss, for the return match under floodlights in Hamilton on Saturday.
Dedicated Travaglini replaces Cristian Viez on the side of the scrum, while Mario Ledesma comes in for hooker Carlos Promanzio and Diego Albanese for winger Tomas Solari.
Two positional switches also have also been made by the Pumas' selectors in an effort to provide some resistance against the awesome All Black rugby machine.

Facundo Soler has been switched to right wing from the left to face Tana Umaga, leaving the vacant other wing spot to Albanese. Rolando Martin moves from blindside flanker to the openside. Travaglini will slot into the blindside of the scrum.
"These three have worked hard for their places and we believe they have earned them," Pumas coach Jose Imhoff said of Albanese, Travaglini and Ledesma, who played 16 minutes of the first test.
Travaglini made his test debut last year against the United States and scored a try in the first five minutes.
"It was a good start," he said.
He never started in another test, going on as replacements against Uruguay and Canada.
"The big three are New Zealand, South Africa and Australia. They are the real test nations," Travaglini said.
"Now I've been given the chance and it'll be up to me, though I wish it was an easier team than the All Blacks. But everyone wants to play the All Blacks and I'm no different."
Albanese takes over from the only player who scored a try against the All Blacks last week -- Solari.
He and Promanzio have been demoted to the bench.
The promotion of Alabanese and Travaglini, both 23, resulted from their performance in Tuesday's 10-26 loss to Taranaki, Pumas coach Jose Imhoff said.
The unlucky player to miss selection was another loose forward, Pablo Bouza, who had two cracker midweek games and still failed to get a test start.
Bouza is a second and middle row utility, which makes him an ideal benchman.
Soler appeared to have paid the price for Umaga's continuous penetration at Athletic Park, though the story was much the same for every other member of Argentina's first test side.

Albanese, a Buenos Aires provincial team-mate of Travaglini and Ledesma, has been capped eight times, including one from the 1995 World Cup match against England, a test against the Springboks and the Twickenham clash last year when the Pumas nearly upset England.
His 1996 season was stalled by a broken arm.

Albanese was one of the three outstanding players, the others being Bouza and Travaglini, against Taranaki and he capped a fine day with a try he and haflback Christian Barrea had hatched on the blindside of scrum inside their own half.
The bearded Travaglini's selection was based on his strong defence against Taranaki, particularly around the fringes where the All Blacks completely outplayed the Pumas in the first test.

Ledesma, 24, has been a steady performer on tour and provided the front row stability against Taranaki. He took three clean tightheads against combined Nelson Bays-Marlborough and one against Taranaki's Shane McDonald, a surprise reserve in one of the All Black trial teams.

Young in terms of a hooker because he only switched there from No 8 last season, Ledesma also played as a flanker on the Pumas tour of England last year when team injuries forced him to pack down on the side of the scrum.

Argentina's second test team: Ezequiel Jurado, Facundo Soler, Eduardo Simone, Diego Albanese, Lisandro Arbizu (captain), Gonzalo Quesada, Fernandez Miranda, Pablo Camerlinckz, Rolanddo Martin, German Llanes, Pedro Sporleder, Roberto Travaglini, Mauricio Reggiardo, Mario Ledesma, Roberto Grau. Reserves: Cristian Barrea, Tomas Solari, one to be decided, Carlo Promanzio, Omar Hasan, Pablo Bouza.
